cases.customer_question: Which hardware or software changes require a new Bluetooth qualification, and which changes can be treated as non-Bluetooth modifications?
question_variants: Do non-Bluetooth software updates require requalification?
Does changing the antenna require a new Bluetooth qualification?
Can PCB changes be ignored if Bluetooth circuitry is unchanged?
Do enclosure changes require RF retesting?
What hardware changes affect Bluetooth qualification status?
Can antenna tuning changes remain under the same listing?
cases.actual_issue: Determining whether design modifications change the qualified Bluetooth Support Layers or ICS-defined functionality enough to require a new qualification instead of derivative product listing.
cases.plain_english_explanation: The customer wanted to know which product changes affect Bluetooth qualification status. Software or hardware changes unrelated to Bluetooth functionality generally do not require requalification. However, antenna changes and RF-related modifications must still be checked to ensure the product remains within the original qualified RF class and performance limits.
cases.consultant_answer: Bluetooth qualification covers the Bluetooth Support Layers and ICS-defined Bluetooth functionality, not unrelated SoC features such as Wi-Fi or unrelated software. Non-Bluetooth software modifications do not require requalification if the registered Bluetooth functionality is unchanged. Antenna changes require RF output and receiver sensitivity verification using a BQTF RF test system. If the modified antenna still satisfies the original qualification class and RF limits, the product can be added as a derivative model to the existing Product List. However, a gain increase can change BR/EDR class compliance, such as causing a Class 2 design to fail and effectively become Class 1, preventing reuse of the original listing. Bluetooth-unrelated circuit changes, such as audio amplifiers, are outside Bluetooth qualification scope if they do not affect Bluetooth RF characteristics. Enclosure changes alone do not require Bluetooth radiated retesting because Bluetooth qualification uses conducted mode testing rather than radiation-mode testing.
cases.decision_logic: The deciding factor is whether the change affects Bluetooth Support Layers, ICS-defined capabilities, or Bluetooth RF characteristics associated with the qualified design. Non-Bluetooth modifications are out of scope, while RF-impacting changes must still satisfy the original qualification conditions.
cases.final_recommendation: Before product updates, verify whether the change affects Bluetooth RF behavior, Support Layers, or ICS-defined features. For antenna or RF-path changes, perform conducted RF verification and confirm the product still meets the original qualification class before reusing the existing listing.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Improperly reusing an existing listing after RF-impacting changes may invalidate the qualification or cause compliance failures. Antenna gain changes can unintentionally shift BR/EDR class compliance and prevent derivative listing eligibility.
